card.name: Words after a stated problem or shortfall
card.fires_on: Ordinary words (an, they, is, recycled, developing) inside a sentence that follows a negative opener such as "Unfortunately" or "The problem with ... is that". It also fires within sentences about something going wrong or falling short.

modes.label: After Unfortunately
modes.description: Words in the clause right after a sentence-opening "Unfortunately", such as the article or verb.
modes.example: Unfortunately, ultra-high-voltage spikes do not represent<< an>> unusual condition.

modes.label: After "The problem is that"
modes.description: A pronoun or verb in the clause after a stated problem with something.
modes.example: The problem with assistive technologies is that<< they>> are often expensive to develop and have a

modes.label: Shortfall or error clause
modes.description: A verb describing something being missed, underestimated, or only partly done.
modes.example: the analysis-error covariance will be<< underestimated>>.

card.writes: It pushes toward words of transparency, reassurance and control, and away from "unfortunately" and words for lack or failure.
card.plain: It lights up in the middle of sentences that are describing a problem or drawback.
